title: Rental replacement by-law and school zone speed limits
subtitle: Winter sidewalk clearing grant, automated speed enforcement hours, and tenant protections against eviction and displacement.
overview: The committee recommended that staff engage the development industry and community groups on a rental replacement by-law, the main item of the meeting. Such a by-law would require replacement of rental units lost to demolition in buildings of six or more units. Staff expect to report back in the first quarter of 2024. The recommendation passed unanimously {{vote:m3}}. A councillor who owns rental property declared a conflict and did not take part.

On school zone speed limits, the committee did not settle the question. It deferred the matter to the December 11 Council meeting {{vote:m2}} so staff can keep talking with the Region of Waterloo about when automated speed cameras operate. Members were split over 40 versus 30 km/h on busier roads and over limiting camera enforcement hours.

The committee also recommended a grant of up to $96,000 a year to The Working Centre for winter sidewalk clearing for residents who need help, subject to annual budget approval {{vote:m1}}. All of these are recommendations that Council will take up later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff engage developers and community stakeholders on a rental replacement by-law (Option 3), keep exploring other tools to support displaced residents, and keep working with the Region of Waterloo.

The committee recommended a grant of up to $96,000 per year to The Working Centre for winter sidewalk clearing, subject to annual budget approval, adjusted for the number of properties served and not usable for subcontracting commercial contractors.
The committee recommended authorizing the General Manager of Infrastructure Services to renew the grant agreement, subject to the City Solicitor's satisfaction.

The committee deferred the proposed 40 km/h limit on major roads and 30 km/h limit on local streets to the December 11 Council meeting so staff can gather more information on automated speed enforcement times.

debate: Staff argued for static school zone limits because school properties are used by the community outside school hours and consistent limits encourage consistent driving. Staff also warned that signed time-of-day limits would prevent cameras from being used and could increase ticket disputes in court.

Several councillors objected to cameras ticketing drivers overnight or on holidays, and favoured limiting enforcement hours, such as 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days, as in the Region's earlier pilot. Others said schoolyards are used by children and families at all hours and that consistent limits build driving habits.

The Mayor questioned whether the busier roads should be 40 km/h, noting staff's figures that pedestrian survival rises with lower speeds. Others wanted 40 km/h everywhere to match the Region. Staff said enforcement hours could be limited behind the scenes without signs, but the Region makes that decision.

Delegates supporting the rental replacement by-law said it would protect affordable units and tenants facing demolition. They asked for no phase-in, no cash in lieu, a right of first refusal for existing tenants, and temporary housing support. They said developers rather than taxpayers should bear the cost.

The consultant said a by-law would add to development costs and could discourage some redevelopment. One councillor asked for economic development support so the by-law does not stall housing supply. Others stressed the need for advocacy to the province on evictions for renovations, which the city cannot regulate.
